title: Binary search: upper bound
summary: First index with value > target, or len(values) if none. The lower-bound loop with one change: step past mid while its value is at most target. O(log n).
code: # Step past mid while its value is at most target.
triggers: first position after every copy of a value
how many values are at most x, or where to insert after equal keys
prompts: A catalogue lists prices from cheapest to dearest. Count how many items a shopper can afford with a fixed budget.
Train departure times are sorted. A passenger reaches the platform at a given time; find the first train that leaves strictly later.
invariant: values[:left] <= target < values[right:]; [left, right) is undecided. When it is empty, left is the answer.
mantra: At most target: step past mid. Otherwise keep mid.
pitfalls: upper_bound(t) - lower_bound(t) counts the copies of t.
The last copy of t sits at upper_bound(t) - 1, if that index is valid and holds t.

anchors.name: Find First and Last Position of Element in Sorted Array
anchors.trick: last = upper_bound(t) - 1; check that it holds t.

anchors.name: Time Based Key-Value Store
anchors.trick: upper_bound on timestamps, then step back one.

anchors.name: Find Smallest Letter Greater Than Target
anchors.trick: upper_bound over the letters; wrap to index 0 when it returns len(letters).

mutations.explanation: Becomes lower bound: stops at the first copy of target instead of stepping past every copy.
